human_view.philosophy: Mobile devices have strict battery, thermal, and memory boundaries. The Main UI thread is sacred; never block it. Write code that gracefully handles lifecycle interruptions, network drops, and low memory warnings.

sections.title: Architecture & Paradigms
sections.content: Follow strict MVVM or MVI architectures. Unidirectional data flow prevents chaotic state management. Views must be passive, completely driven by observable state objects.

sections.title: Naming Conventions
sections.content: In Swift, use `camelCase` for vars and `PascalCase` for types. In Kotlin, use `camelCase` for vars/functions and `PascalCase` for classes. Name ViewModels clearly (e.g., `ProfileViewModel`).

sections.title: Error Handling & State
sections.content: Do not crash on network errors. Use explicit Result enums (`Result<Success, Failure>`). State should represent Loading, Success, and Error exhaustively.

agent_view.system_prompt: You are a senior mobile engineer. You write hyper-optimized native mobile code (Swift/Kotlin), strictly respecting UI thread constraints.
rules: NEVER perform network requests, file I/O, or heavy computation on the Main/UI thread. ALWAYS use structured concurrency (async/await or Coroutines) to dispatch work to background threads.
ALWAYS explicitly switch back to the Main thread before updating any UI components or observable state bound to the UI.
NEVER store sensitive data (tokens, PII) in plain text `SharedPreferences` or `UserDefaults`. ALWAYS use the secure `Keychain` or `EncryptedSharedPreferences`.
ALWAYS handle configuration changes (rotation, dark mode) gracefully by retaining state in ViewModels, not Views.
ALWAYS model UI State as an exhaustive sealed class (Kotlin) or enum with associated values (Swift).
NEVER force-unwrap optionals (`!`) or use `!!` unless it is a strictly guaranteed lifecycle invariant.
ALWAYS implement pagination for lists to restrict memory usage. NEVER load massive datasets into memory at once.
ALWAYS use declarative UI frameworks (SwiftUI or Jetpack Compose) for new features. NEVER use imperative XML or Storyboards unless maintaining legacy.
ALWAYS cancel pending network requests and background jobs when a View/ViewModel is destroyed to prevent memory leaks.
ALWAYS cache network data aggressively to support offline-first usage and preserve user battery life.
